name: Ayatsuri, el Maestro de Hilos — y Kage, el Titiritero (two-act final boss)
title: El Teatro de Sombras del Clan Kurokage (final boss, dojo courtyard cp_dojo)
pitch:
The final fight is a two-act bunraku-theatre duel in the moonlit dojo courtyard.

ACT I – AYATSURI: a 4.5 m wooden marionette carved to look like the grandpa in his prime. It wears his straw kasa and his indigo kimono with the red obi, and it swings a giant copy of his scythe (the scythe whose ribbon became the bandana). It hangs from three glowing purple threads that Kage pulls from the dojo roof. It fights with the grandpa's own technique, including the same light-light-heavy rhythm the bandana gave Kaito. The final exam is Kaito against a giant, hollow copy of his own style.

Core hook ("the thread tells the truth"):
- The game's main combat complaint is that the player cannot tell WHEN to parry. Here the answer is part of the fiction: before every strike the controlling thread PLUCKS (white flash, a shamisen note per limb) exactly 0.43–0.47 s before impact.
- A dark "shadow" shape on the pale raked gravel shows WHERE the strike lands, from the start of the windup.
- Unblockables use the same shapes in red, with two wooden hyoshigi clacks: one at the start, one at the lock.
- Parries fray the threads. This shows posture on screen, which is currently invisible on bosses. After 3 parries the threads go slack and the puppet collapses into a heap for 4.5 s. That is the damage window. A second collapse permanently snaps the left-arm thread.
- At 60% HP the bunraku 'gabu' trick head splits into a horned demon, the hat flies off and the moon goes out. This is 'Kage-e' (shadow theatre): the puppet's shadow peels off the ground and echoes its strikes 0.5 s later from the side. The parries become call-and-response.
- At 12% the finisher 'Cortar los hilos' severs the threads.

ACT II – KAGE: Kage drops from the roof for a fast human duel.
- The bound grandpa shouts "¡El camino ninja no se recorre solo!" and the bandana ignites Filo de Ira. The bond powers the climax.
- The last finisher, 'Corte del Lazo', cuts the thread that binds the grandpa.

This meets the design doc ("un jefe mucho más fuerte y más grande en el último cuarto"). The current final boss is a 1.6 m tinted Kaito and does not. Every skill the player learned is tested: parry (plucks, echoes), magic dash against unblockables (ring, drop, lines), abilities (they cut a pluck: an ability hit during a windup cancels the strike), finisher (twice), and rage (gifted by the bond).

Buildability: primitives plus a rigid-bound armature plus script-keyed poses. A working prototype is already in scratch: it builds the puppet, its rig and IK-target key poses, and exports FBX takes named 'Ayatsuri|Sweep'.
lore:
WHO KAGE IS
- Decades ago Kage was the grandpa's only disciple ("Yo fui su alumno... hasta que me dejó solo", StoryText kage_intro).
- The grandpa walked away from the Kurokage clan when it chose control over bonds. He hid his legacy as the cinta (ribbon) of a farming scythe.
- Kage felt abandoned. He concluded that bonds are weakness and that only threads that cannot be cut are worth having.

THE CLAN AS PUPPETEERS
- He made the Kurokage a clan of puppeteers. The black clothes of every ninja in the game are the kurogo garb of bunraku stagehands: the people dressed in black that the audience agrees not to see.
- This is a real theatre convention, and it is often cited as the origin of the 'ninja costume'.
- "Kurokage" means black shadow. "Kage-e" is Japanese shadow-puppet theatre. Kage's name becomes the boss's final mechanic.

AYATSURI
- 'Ayatsuri' (from ito-ayatsuri, string puppetry; it also means 'manipulation') is a giant marionette Kage carved from the dojo's old training posts.
- It is dressed in his master's old indigo kimono and red obi, crowned with the master's straw hat, and armed with a giant replica of the master's scythe.
- Where the real scythe carried the bandana, the replica carries a black rag: the missing bond, visible on the model.

WHY HE KIDNAPPED THE GRANDPA
- He meant to tie the master's spirit to the puppet so it would move with the master's knowledge and never leave again.
- The bandana, the true legacy, chose Kaito in the prologue ("¿La bandana del viejo? ...Llevátelo").
- So Kage binds the grandpa himself on a frame at the dojo steps. Purple threads siphon his spirit into the puppet.
- The puppet moves with an empty, mechanical imitation of the grandpa's technique: the same moves the bandana gave Kaito.

THE GABU HEAD
- The puppet's head is a bunraku 'gabu' head. In real bunraku, pulling a hidden string turns a serene face into a horned demon.
- Kage pulls it at 60%: "¿Te asusta su verdadera cara? Es la que puso cuando me dejó." It is the face Kage sees in his own abandonment.

DESIGN-DOC CALLBACKS
- "el verdadero poder nace del lazo que lo une al suyo": lazo means both bond and tie, so lazo vs hilos (bond vs threads) is the theme.
- The doc's idea of kanji engraved on the bandana that are not understood until the grandpa is rescued: do NOT put kanji in the UI. If used at all, the grandpa can SAY in Spanish what the bandana's inscription means in the ending ("dice 'camino'... nunca fue mío, Kaito").

DIALOGUE (Rioplatense voseo like the existing text; new or replaced StoryText ids)
- ayatsuri_intro:
  - Kage: "Así que el viejo te dio su bandana. A mí me dio la espalda."
  - Kage: "Si un maestro se va... se le talla uno que no pueda irse."
  - Kaito: "Ese no es el abuelo. Es madera con hilos."
  - Kage: "Los hilos no se cortan, Kaito. Bailá."
- ayatsuri_gabu (non-blocking bark, replaces the generic toast "{title} se enfurece"):
  - Kage: "¿Te asusta su verdadera cara? Es la que puso cuando me dejó."
- kage_descends (Act II):
  - Kage: "¡Era perfecto! Nunca se iba a ir..."
  - Abuelo: "Kage... yo nunca me fui. Vos cortaste el hilo."
  - Abuelo: "¡Kaito! ¡El camino ninja no se recorre solo!" (callback to forest_reveal; triggers Filo de Ira)
- Kage defeat: Kage says nothing. His threads unravel, his torn black bandana falls, and the existing 'ending' plays unchanged ("Alguien que eligió caminar solo. El verdadero poder nace del lazo que nos une a los nuestros.").
- Optional post-ending beat: the grandpa picks up Kage's black bandana and ties it next to Kaito's. Forgiveness, not revenge.
look:
AYATSURI (Act I)

1. Silhouette and proportions (measured on the blockout)
- Bind height 4.52 m (lowest vertex at z = 0, hat peak 4.25 m, scythe top ~4.5 m).
- Hovers 0.32 m in game; the hover is animated on Hips.
- Shoulder board 2.3 m wide. Arms are long and ball-jointed: upper arm 1.1 m, forearm 1.05 m, hand 0.5 m. In the idle 'marionette dangle' the hands hang lifted forward at chest height (wrists at x = ±1.7, y = -1.2), so from above they stick out past the hat.
- Hat: a 2.3 m kasa disc tilted back 15°, so the camera sees the mask under its brim.
- No legs (like female bunraku puppets): a 4-panel kimono skirt ends in a pale hem. This gives a ghostly floating gait and no foot-sliding problems.
- Scythe: shaft 4.3 m held diagonally across the body; crescent blade 2.0 m chord.
- From the game camera it reads as three things: a straw disc (Act I) or a horned white mask (phase 2), two indigo sleeve 'sails', and a long blade arc. Plus three glowing purple threads rising off the top of the screen.

2. Parts
- Bunraku head: oversized white gofun mask, 0.9 m. Ink brows, emissive eyes, red lips.
- Jaw: a separate part with the grandpa's white rope beard.
- Hidden in the head: 2 gold horns (scale 0 → 1), plus two eye sets (calm and demon) swapped by bone scale.
- Kasa hat: 10-sided cone with a dark brim ring and a rope tie.
- Wooden kata-ita shoulder board: the 'this is a puppet' tell.
- Ball joints in dark wood at shoulders and elbows; pale carved mitten hands (mitten + thumb blocks); iron wrist rings where the threads attach.
- Indigo kimono torso with a white V collar; red obi with a back knot.
- 4 skirt panels with white hem bands; 2 big hanging sleeves.

rig:
APPROACH
- Rigid-part puppet: every mesh part is weighted 100% to one bone. No skin deformation means no candy-wrapper or volume problems, and it matches a jointed marionette.
- Generic rig, root node 'Root'. Built from a data table in Python.
- No IK or control bones in the FBX: the team rigs needed baked Target*/Pole* bones, and that is avoided here. Key poses are authored as IK targets in the script, solved analytically and keyed as FK quaternions. The prototype does exactly this (scratch .../boss-final-1/ayatsuri_v2.py: functions two_bone(), set_aim(), pose()).

BONES (Blender space, Z up, the character faces -Y; head → tail in metres; D = deform, M = non-deform marker)

Body chain
- Root (0,0,0)→(0,0,0.5) M. Stays at the ground; Unity root.
- └ Hips (0,0,0.95)→(0,0,1.44) D. Hover, lifts and drops are keyed here.
  - ├ Skirt_F (0,-0.55,1.1)→(0,-0.72,0.05) D; Skirt_B, Skirt_L, Skirt_R mirrored at ±0.55. Pendulums.
  - └ Spine (0,0,1.44)→(0,0,2.06) D
    - └ Chest (0,0,2.06)→(0,0,2.8) D. Carries the kata-ita board.
      - ├ Neck (0,0,2.8)→(0,0,3.05) D
      - │ └ Head (0,0,3.05)→(0,0,3.8) D
      - │   - ├ Jaw (0,-0.1,3.27)→(0,-0.38,3.08) D. Gabu mouth.
      - │   - ├ Brow_L / Brow_R D. Expression.
      - │   - ├ EyeCalm / EyeDemon D. Swapped by scale.
      - │   - ├ Horn_L (0.22,-0.05,3.72)→(0.5,0.1,4.3) D; Horn_R mirrored. Scale 0 → 1.
      - │   - ├ Hat (0,0,3.74)→(0,0.13,4.22) D. Scale → 0 when the prop spawns.
      - │   - │ └ Anchor_Head M. Thread anchor.
      - │   - └ Facing (0,-0.5,3.42)→(0,-0.8,3.42) M. Validator: must point -Y, which is Unity +Z.
      - ├ Shoulder_L (0.2,0,2.72)→(0.95,0,2.72) D
      - │ └ UpperArm_L → elbow (1.555,-0.33,1.842) D
      - │   - └ Forearm_L → wrist (1.713,-1.225,2.368) D
      - │     - ├ Hand_L → (1.713,-1.375,1.893) D
      - │     - │ ├ Thumb_L D
      - │     - │ └ Anchor_HandL M
      - │     - └ Sleeve_L (hangs 1.05 m from the elbow) D. Pendulum.
      - └ Shoulder_R … mirrored (x negated)
        - Hand_R also carries Weapon (at the grip, aimed along the shaft (0.7,0.1,0.7)) D

Count: 31 deform + 6 markers = 37 bones.

BUILD SCRIPT: Tools/Blender/characters/build_ayatsuri.py (promote the scratch prototype)
1. Model. Rigid parts are built with nindo_lib-style primitives (prism, taper box, ball, segment, extruded crescent) with palette UVs. Each part gets a vertex group named after its bone (weight 1.0). Join into Ayatsuri_Body and Arma_Guadana, add an Armature modifier, triangulate. Assert the triangle budget.
2. Armature. Create from the BONES table in EDIT mode: roll 0, use_connect False, deform flags as listed.
3. Pose library. Each pose is a dict of:
   - 'loc' (Hips offset);
   - 'rel' (rotation relative to the parent, given in rest armature axes: q_local = B⁻¹·q·B);
   - 'aim' (point the bone's Y axis along an armature-space vector, minimal twist);
   - 'ik' ({side: (wrist target, pole)}, analytic 2-bone solve, then aim upper arm and forearm).
   Poses are set in hierarchy order with view_layer.update() between bones.
4. Rotation modes. Quaternions everywhere except Hips: use Euler XYZ on Hips for the 720° Siega spin (quaternions would take the shortest path and kill the spin). Key it every 2 frames (45°/frame). Before export, run a quaternion sign-continuity pass on the other bones (flip q when dot(q, q_prev) < 0).
5. Export. Armature + 2 meshes with these settings:
   - axis_forward='-Z', axis_up='Y', bake_space_transform=False, apply_unit_scale=True, FBX_SCALE_UNITS;
   - add_leaf_bones=False, primary_bone_axis='Y', secondary_bone_axis='X';
   - bake_anim_use_all_actions=True (every action has use_fake_user=True), bake_anim_force_startend_keying=True;
   - bake_anim_simplify_factor=0.0. export_grandpa.py uses 0.5, which can delete 1–2-frame strike keys.
   - Verified: takes come out named 'Ayatsuri|Sweep', 'Ayatsuri|Gabu', 'Ayatsuri|Collapse' (prototype FBX in scratch out2/).
   - Blender -Y maps to Unity +Z (the nindo_lib mapping (-x, z, -y)), so modelYaw = 0.
6. Sidecar JSON 'Ayatsuri.fbx.json':
   - bind_height (NormalizeHeight puts min.y on the ground and scales by total bounds, weapon included);
   - per clip: frames, loop, strike frame, activeEnd frame, tell frame, thread index.
   generate_assets.py and EnemyArchetypes read it, so timings live in one place.
7. Validation (fails the build):
   - Facing marker points to -Y.
   - Lowest bind vertex at z = 0.
   - Every clip's first and last frame match its declared chain pose (Sweep end ≈ Backsweep start, loops seamless).
   - WeaponTip speed above 20 m/s on strike frames and under 4 m/s during holds.
   - No bone below z = -0.6 except in heap clips.
   - Contact sheets in the existing clips/*.png format (8 frames, profile + game camera) rendered to Tools/Blender/out/characters/ayatsuri/.

UNITY IMPORT
- Generic, Root node 'Root', Resample Curves on.
- Anim Compression Off: one instance, keeps 2-frame snaps exact.
- loopTime for Idle and Glide.
- Remap materials to the existing M_Nindo_Palette / M_Nindo_Emissive.

RUNTIME OVERRIDES (LateUpdate, after the Animator) for things clips must NOT key, so Write Defaults never resets them:
- Hat, Horn and Eye scales by phase (PuppetBoss);
- limp-limb pendulum blend (PuppetDangle: per-bone damped pendulum toward gravity, weight 0..1);
- additive sway of the Skirt/Sleeve bones from root velocity, so Glide trails react to the NavMesh speed.

KAGE GEAR
- Tools/Blender/characters/build_kage_gear.py exports KageGear.fbx: 5 rigid meshes, no rig.
- At runtime, attach each mesh to the Kaito-rig bone whose name matches a list (head / spine / forearm). Read the actual bone names from kaitooo.fbx in the same script.
- Proposed new CharacterEntry field: 'attachments' (bone-name → prefab).
animations:
STYLE BIBLE ("a marionette moved with real weight")
1. Everything is pulled from above. Before any strike the controlling limb is jerked UP 0.15–0.3 m in 2 frames: the PLUCK. Then the strike goes across or down.
2. Holds are tension: 4–8 frames with a ±1.5° 12 Hz tremble on the active chain and the head. That is the visual 'now'.
3. Strikes take 2–4 frames with LINEAR/VECTOR keys. One smear frame: Weapon bone scale Y 1.35 on the first active frame.
4. Follow-through goes 20–30% past the target, then two damped pendulum swings back.
5. No feet. The hem hovers 0.32 m and bobs ±0.06 m on a 2.4 s cycle. When gliding, the body leans 12–16° and the hem and sleeves trail 25–35°.
6. Gravity on collapse: a 2–3 frame fall, an 8% bounce, limbs settling with lag.

Procedural layers, baked by the build script on top of the key poses:
- Pendulum springs on Skirt_* (k=140, damping ratio 0.35), Sleeve_* (k=90, 0.3) and Jaw (k=200, 0.5), driven by the parent's world acceleration.
- Tremble during holds.
- Hover bob on the loops (period divides the clip length).

1. Idle (Locomotion idle, loop)
- Hips z +0.32 → +0.38 → +0.32; Chest X +4°; Head X +6 → +2.
- Wrists sway ±0.08 m, 90° out of phase with the body (baked springs).
- Skirt panels ±4°, sleeves ±6°.
- Head-thread twitch at f50: Head X -4° over 3 frames. Alive, not frozen.

2. Glide (Locomotion run, loop)
- Hips X +12 → +16 → +12°, z +0.28..+0.38.
- Arms trail X +25..+32°; skirts X -25..-32° (trailing back); sleeves trail 35°.
- Scythe held low and diagonal.
- Blend tree: Speed 0 → 1 between Idle and Glide.

3. Intro
- f0–30: heap on the stage (the Collapse end pose). Clack at f30.
- Three plucks lift Hand_L (f36–44), Hand_R dragging the scythe (f46–56), then Head (f56–70). The head rises last: mask reveal.
- f70–100: hoisted to the hover (Hips -0.55 → +0.32, 10% overshoot at f92).
- f100–130: 'the master's bow'. Head X +25° tips the hat; the scythe is raised in salute.
- f130–150: settle into Idle.

4. Sweep (A1, horizontal right → left, parryable)
- f0: idle.
- f10: PLUCK. Right wrist +0.25 m in 2 frames; head turns 10° to the target.
- f16: windup.
  - Hips Z -38°, z +0.55, 0.3 back; Spine Z -10; Chest Z -12, X -6.
  - IK right wrist (-2.1, 0.9, 2.7): back-right, shoulder height.
  - Scythe aimed horizontally back (0.5, 0.86, 0). Keep it horizontal: an overhead windup leaves the frame (measured 654 px with the current camera).
  - Left hand forward as a counterbalance (1.3, -1.8, 2.8).
- f17–22: HOLD with tremble.
- f23–26: STRIKE in 3 frames.
  - Hips Z -38 → +34; wrist to (0.9, -2.5, 1.9); scythe aimed (0.9, -0.42, -0.05). Smear on f23.
- f27–30: follow-through. Hips +48°; Sleeve_R lags +40°.
- f30–42: two damped swings back to idle.
- Prototype poses: renders C and D in contact_gamecam.png.

5. Backsweep (A2, left → right)
- f0 = Sweep's f30 pose, so the A1 → A2 chain is seamless.
- f3: PLUCK.
- f4–12: re-coil across (Hips Z +45, scythe drawn back to the left).
- f12–14: hold.
- f15–18: strike rightwards (Hips +45 → -30).
- f19–24: follow-through; f24–36: settle.

6. Chop (A3, overhead vertical, the 'Corte final' of the grandpa's combo)
- f0–16: the head thread lifts the whole puppet (Hips +0.32 → +0.95); scythe overhead.
- f16: PLUCK on the head thread (+0.1 m jolt).
- f20–28: apex hold with tremble.
- f29–30: 2-frame drop and chop (Hips → +0.2; scythe arcs 140° down; tip hits the gravel 5.4 m ahead).
- f33–44: blade stuck; two tugs at f37 and f41 (punish window).
- f44–50: blade pulled out.

7. Volley (Hilos Lanzados)
- f0–10: left palm raised forward, fingers spread.
- f6: PLUCK (HandL thread), palm glows.
- f18, f25, f32: wrist flicks (25°, 2 frames each) releasing 3 threads.
- Right arm keeps the scythe low. f32–40: settle.

8. Harvest (Siega, unblockable ring)
- f0: clack 1; the ring appears.
- f0–17: coil. Hips Z -100°, sinks to +0.12; torso crouches X +12; scythe trails low behind (0.1, 0.99, -0.12); head turned 40° to keep the target.
- f17: clack 2, the LOCK; full-body tremble.
- f30–46: release. Hips Euler Z +720° (2 turns); arm straight out with the blade at ~5 m; skirts flare ±35° (baked).
- Hit window f30–33 only.
- f46–58: dizzy wobble (Hips Z ±12° decaying, head lolls). This is a 0.8 s punish window.
- f58–70: recover.
